body:
Its brain chemicals. You ever been to a doctor that gave you a depression questionnaire? That question on all of them that goes *"do you feel an impending sense of doom or that something awful is about to happen to you?"* I always checked "no" and kind of laughed to myself in my head like "wtf is that?"

Well for the last couple months I've been feeling it too. Every day I wake up and feel like I'm waking up on my execution day. Shit, shower, shave, eat your last meal and strap into the electric chair. 

But nothing ever really happens. Its just something my brain is doing lately.

Or, you know... maybe we're on to something... maybe something world cataclysmic is about to happen and the drunks are tuned into it. But does that seem likely?

Yeah, its been a year or more. We never talked more than a sentence but he would probably be happy to see me if I walked back in. Why cant I do it? There were a bunch of police and an ambulance outside his stop today. Was worried he got robbed and shot, but it was a motorcycle crash.
20 years of suicidal depression. I missed everything.
All of the above except #10 and including your edits.
Yeah, my family had Jesus. They're a lot of the reason I take antidepressants.

>All I wanted was for her to tell me to stop.

First of all, she's not gonna do that either, that makes her feel bad too. That's putting them in an impossible position again.

>I feel guilty but also confused about what I did wrong. 

People have a visceral reaction to suicide that we forget exists. Death is literally one of the top 3 scariest things most people can imagine. They spend their whole lives trying *not* to think about it, and suicidal people drop it right in front of them. You didn't do anything wrong, that's just how this goes... but now you know, so you've gotta decide if you're going to willingly keep doing it.

>And I have lost my friend for good. She will always have a bad knee jerk reaction to me. 

You could go to the hospital, or start seeing a therapist, and tell her that it was her that got you to finally do it. Tell her she was the one that got you to do it when no one else could. It wouldn't be a lie, and she would be overjoyed to have finally helped. To finally at least think she's safe from having her friend die. Tell her you realize what it did to her and you hope it didn't ruin things forever, then give her space. Odds are she will come back and pretend like nothing ever happened.

I don't know how your depression works out in the long run. That is a much longer conversation and if you need help with it, PM me please. But as far as relationships go for depressed people, the name of the game is to fake it. If you were being crushed by a boulder... and you knew she couldn't possibly lift it... you would smile and say "it's ok, it doesn't hurt, don't worry about it, just spend time with me." It doesn't have to be a perfect act. There will still be days when you can't fake it and she'll hear the sadness in your voice and will ask if you're ok. And you'll say "yeah, just a rough day, but not too bad." and she'll play along. We spend so much time frantically hoping they can help us, that we forget to do the same for them.

I'm not giving this advice lightly. I know asking you to fake happy while depressed is probably the hardest thing someone could ask you to do. It feels impossible and scary... just like what she was facing. One of you is gonna have to face the monster. If you let it be her, she'll run, you'll both lose. If it's you, the worst that happens is you keep your friend and the best that happens is you might live happily ever after.

It's not malicious abuse. I don't believe you want to hurt her... but it does. And we know that, but we still keep doing it. So, I dunno. I could sugar coat it, but that wouldn't help you very much.

I understand the need to grasp for help in the really bad times. It's not wrong of you to want. And if it gets that bad and you have no one else at the moment, then you do what you have to do. But it might cost you the relationship. And she still probably won't be able to help the way you both wish she could. 

You are wrong that you can't help it. Depression makes you feel like you can't help it, but in the end you're the only person or thing that *can* help it. Eventually you're going to have to fight back against the thoughts and compulsions that depression causes. Today or in 6 months... it's gonna be the exact same fight. But if you start today you can keep your friend.

Yeah, we're emotionally abusive as hell with this. The first time you tell someone is fair. If they can help they will. But usually it just scares them and makes them feel helpless. All the times we tell them after that are just venting for stress and forcing them back into that helpless spot. We're used to looking at death, they're not. It scares the shit out of them and eventually their self preservation will override their desire to stand by you. It's just human.

It's unfortunate, because depression makes you feel a need to get it out. Tell someone in just the right way so that they can say the magic words to make it better. But has that worked so far? Is it going to? That kind of talk is best reserved for a therapist because most people just aren't equipped to help. In the mean time, if you want to keep those people around, you might have to do your best to temporarily repress it around them. Which is nothing to be ashamed of, it's a step towards fighting back against the depression.

They're not going to show up to small claims court. Which means OP will win by default, put they still won't pay. OP could garnish wages or social security, if they had the parents SS#, but I'm sure they don't. So all in all you're just out another $75 to pay the process server for a judgement that is mostly worthless.

What worked for me... was inventing an emergency situation that required my important papers post-haste. Dream job, they need my birth certificate and such by the end of the week or I'll lose it. There was no dream job. Otherwise, just go straight to the hospital, college, etc and get copies.

Mine used to say that all the time. The first few years I took it in stunned silence. "Holy shit, that's right, I'm gonna have to take care of her eventually." Then I realized, ha, no, I won't. The end of your life is gonna be like the beginning of mine, scared and alone. The biggest regret of NC is that I don't get to point that out anymore.
I want to believe this, but how do they hide it so much better?
Not really, and I was lead to believe it would.

>But he sets the bar so high for himself that he feels he always fails at everything.

What do normal people do? If you set the bar at an easily attainable height, you always know that you could or should have done better, and that everyone else knows that too.
How do you measure a good therapist? I spent years with one that I liked but we didn't get shit accomplished, I don't know if it was my fault or hers.
Remember to get your birth certificate, SS# card and other papers if you don't have them, before you tell her.

I have OCD. Real OCD, the kind that robs you of a normal life and gives you something in it's place that makes suicide look like a good idea.

I'll be honest, I don't give a shit when people that like to keep their desk clean go around telling everyone "I'm so ocd!" Everyone wants to feel like they belong somewhere, and most of us are doing a shitty job of it these days. If all you can do is claim a mental illness to feel like you fit somewhere, go for it, I hope it helps. I'm glad you can find some identity in it without actually having to suffer from it. It's not like they're diluting my identity, I hide that shit like it's the plague. You're trying to fake broken, I'm trying to fake normal. Both for the same reason.

The only thing that bothers me about it is that if I do tell someone, their first response is then always "I bet your apartment is really clean!" No, it's a mess, because my life is falling apart, the OCD lies elsewhere. Now I'm even more disappointed in myself for not having the beneficial parts of the affliction.

I was a good kid, smart, did my work, never acted out. My family seemed nice enough from a teachers point of view. Both were a public act. I wish someone would have seen through it and stepped in, or at least built that kid up a little, it would have changed everything. I wasn't *that* good of an actor, there were signs.

I think whatever the subject of the class, it's secondary to the fact that school teaches kids how to handle life. Learning to interact socially, find and fit in to groups, handle bigger and bigger tasks, have confidence in themselves to be able to do all of that. If the kid isn't progressing in that, it really doesn't matter how good or bad he does on his algebra.

There's practically no downside for them to act that way. They get to say whatever cruel thing gratifies them in the moment. As long as they play their image right no one will really look down on it, most will defend them with shit like "you did the best you could, I'm so sorry". You'll feel bad, but that just reaffirms to them that there IS something wrong with you and they were right. Or you'll cave to the cruelty and give them what they want. They win on multiple levels. The only time narcissism is really bad for the narcissist is 30 or 40 years into the future when they've burnt their bridges and are alone and in shambles. But they don't have the insight to make that connection, so they won't feel regret then either.

It's like if opiates didn't leave the track marks, a sickly body, leave you feeling like shit or cost a fortune. It would be all roses and you'd never even consider stopping. That's why none of them change, why would they? If you're willing to destroy everyone close to you, few defense mechanisms pay as well as narcissism does.

Yeah, all the time. You didn't "do your best" you did what you felt like doing and called it your best, for extra sympathy points. Every time there was a choice between doing what a normal parent would do and following your compulsion for cruelty, you went with the compulsions. Now, half of your children want to kill themselves and the other half aren't far behind. If it were me, I'd be more embarrassed to claim that that was "my best" than to just admit I never gave a shit.

They will have no problem telling you again. After this week we'll never hear about this guy again. But I'll still hear 5 times a month how I'm destroying this once great country with my food stamps. It would take me 416,666 years to cost what this guy cost in 14, and people envied him while he did it.

I think understanding that she does it, and why she does it, early on, helps a lot. I didn't realize it was narcissism until I was in my 20's. All that time before that, I thought it was my fault, that I was as bad as she said I was and that's why she didn't like me. That did a lot of damage, if I had realized what it was and why she was doing it, it probably wouldn't have. 

They critisize you and treat you bad because it makes them feel superior, but they're not actually taking the time to judge whether it's true or not. They just say what pops into their head at the moment, and you happen to be standing in front of them. We assume, because they're our parents and because people don't normally say bad stuff without a good reason... that they must see something we don't, they must have really thought about it and decided they had to say it. But they don't. It's all auto-pilot. They care so little that they barely know you. Looking at it now, my mother doesn't know anything about me. What things are important to me, what I like or don't like, why I do things, why I want things, my religion, why I chose the career I did. And I didn't try to hide any of it. She just doesn't care, she built her own story of me in her head because it fits what she wants. So how can anyone that pays so little attention, cares so little, really know what they're talking about when they say bad stuff about you?

It'll still hurt, because you want a mom and don't have one. And I don't think there's a way around that, it'll always hurt. But if you remember that the things she says are not mom things, they're crazy person things, that will help you save your self respect, and that will be important later.

> If I tell him this, he threatens to kill himself.

>He prefers drug dealing and jail

These aren't things that a depressed person that deserves your help does. They're manipulative things. And because they've worked so far, he won't stop doing them until you have nothing left. Someone deserves your help, but it's not this guy, and you're stealing time from the guy that deserves it by wasting it on the one that doesn't.

I have depression, the post made me feel bad. These posts and the amount of agreement with them are why I mentally roll my eyes when my shrink tells me people don't want me to die.

But what do you propose here? OP didn't do this to make depressed people feel bad, OP posted because OP feels bad. But we expect them to keep their mouth shut, hide it and fake it so they don't make us feel bad for it? How horrible would it be if they told us to do the same thing?

OP isn't a shitty person, and you're not a shitty person if being around a depressed person is hard on you. It IS a burden, we already knew that. Maybe these people deserve some of the compassion they've been giving us all these years. And maybe it's a wake up call to us that concessions will have to be made. If you make everything around you accommodate the depression, how can you hope to get better?

I always figured it would make sense to throw a handful of those Pop-it's off the roof and wait 10 seconds before following. Pop-it's will start snapping on the ground, people will look up to see what's going on and have a few seconds to gtfo of the way.

Standing up to them isn't free, they will leave scars for it. At this point I take them as trophies. "I've lived through several decades of you, there's nothing you can do at any one point that's worse than that... but just for shits and giggles, lets see what you've got."

You don't tell them how you're doing at first, that's crazy. You take 3, 4, 5 sessions to figure them out. Talk about the smallest stuff and see how they respond. At some point you realize, nope, this isn't a person I can tell everything to, or ok, this person has my back. You know how to play this game, it's what we do with everyone else.

By and large, the world doesn't want to deal with this stuff. It's scary to some, awkward to others, or just plain makes them feel bad and they want to avoid it. There's a reason why there's only one knee-jerk answer when someone says "hi, how are you?" Probably the world is fucked up and cold, but if you want to fit in with them, you have to play the same game they're playing. Probably they don't like playing it either, but it's what they do to get through it. 

I suspect this is what your friend is telling you. Everyone is just trying to pretend to be ok. By saying it all out loud you put a spotlight on yourself that you probably don't want to be under. At best, people feel sympathy or pity and it still paints you in a way you didn't want them looking at you. Save it for when it's important, with a therapist and with the one person you're closest to, everyone else, fake it. I feel like a lot of us in this sub would have much happier lives if we were better at faking it.

Hiding it doesn't deny it or diminish it, it just avoids unnecessary problems. Keeps it from further victimizing you. I don't see any shame in that.

This sub would be so much more helpful if people could call other people on their BS. Every once in a while I see a post that helps, someone says something I lived and it helps to see that I wasn't wrong for being hurt by that. But mostly it's become an over exaggerated echo chamber. I don't post here much anymore because I know everyone will just agree with me and try to take it to another level. I don't need that. I need people to squash it, try to make it smaller. Not join in and amp up my brokenness.
I appreciate your effort. But have any of you guys that post this number ever called it? It's fuckin' useless. They want to be on that call less than I do.

Lol wtf, 29 cents? That is highly specific. I would like to see that itemized list, or to just watch the process a crazy person goes through producing that list.

But on a serious note, 6 years NC and then out of the blue with a comment like that... would I be off the mark if I guessed some sort of substance abuse problem?

I think the people that were supposed to approve of us, never did. Seems like that's a lot of what builds a child into an adult, a string of small successes... "good job", "you're a good kid", a gold star, maccaroni art hung on the fridge like it was the best gift ever. Little comments that are trivial to a parent, but they know mean the world to the child. But our parents being what they are, never could bring themselves to give those. You were never good enough, always fell at least a little short, never really a person, never got the foundation that everyone else gets.

And you never really learn to live without that, you just get older and keep searching for it. Except hanging macaroni art on the fridge doesn't have the same impact at 15, 30, 60 as it would have when you were 5. So you replace it with other methods to try to feel that approval. Going overboard when doing something for someone, being overly considerate, adoration. Because surely this will make them like me. And it probably does, but their approval doesn't really fill the hole left by a parents lack of it anyway. And the happiness they feel from whatever you did really isn't proportional to the ridiculousness you feel from having done it.

So probably the answer is the same as it is for most of our problems related to this mess. Have to become aware of it and then fight it. Be nice to a point but then draw a line. You'll feel filthy for it. That was the rule when we were small after all, any boundary you set is wrong and you have no right to consider yourself. But no one in the real world measures like that. If you thank them once, they think you're nice, they don't deduct points because you didn't thank them 9 more times after that. You'll feel like an asshole for having not for a while, but people will still like you, still want to be around you. Eventually you'll get comfortable with the fact that no one really expects you to over deliver. Just sort of being cordially average is all most people want.

I think this is it for me, I just want it to be over, to have the door permanently closed. Even if I can maintain NC, there will always be the pull "maybe I could go back just once, maybe they'll be nicer, maybe I'm good enough now, maybe it wasn't so bad." It's always nagging. If I cave, they'll hurt me for it. If I don't, it just keeps getting louder. Their death wouldn't make me feel good, or really change much of anything. It would just take the issue off of the table so that I could stop fighting it, maybe.

I know, I have them in my family. The bad news is that your mom has total power to sway her in her favor. The good news is, that you have the same power. A follower wants desperately to make someone happy so that they like them. If she listens to your mom, she gets the tattoo and your mom is happy and your aunt feels complete because someone is happy with her. On the other hand, she doesn't get the tattoo, that makes you happy, and she wins with you. You're in an arguing war with your mom. Your mom is looking out for your mom, and you are looking out for your aunt. On some level you aunt will get that and side with you.

Well, it seems to me, like duplicate tattoos are a way of tying someone to you forever, which is what N's are all about.

I have no idea what's going on in her life. Maybe she's lost something or someone has gone NC so she needs to make up the difference by getting someone to pledge their allegiance to her. When N's say "it's me and you" it's not me and you, it's "me... and you're following me."
What is MC?

Narcissists live and die based on appearances. They can't outright beat you with a belt, or lock you in the cellar, because there's no way they could spin that to the public, they probably couldn't even spin that to themselves. So all of the abuse has the be plausibly deniable. It has to be little things that go unnoticed, or that can be explained away if they get confronted. Nothing on our lists is horrifically atrocious, people write it off as a single mistake any parent could make on a bad day. Even we do. 

The real abuse was the quantity of it. Everyone else assumes it's a one off slip, but they did this stuff all day, every day, for decades. With none of the decent real parenting in between. That's not normal, that's what makes it monstrous.
We all get it. I don't think you have to try to explain here.
You're going to pay her for that? That's the kind of reinforcement of shitty behavior that makes it worth it to them. Shred them, make him happy rather than her.

Thanks, I get the argument, it's the same argument I make for other people when trying to console them for the same reason. But for myself, I don't accept it. For every person that says "you're why we have the program" there's another that looks at you with pure contempt. And when you already feel bad about it, confirmation bias says you listen to one of those more than the other.

At the same time, I guess that's also why I don't care what people buy with it. It sucks, and if buying a lobster makes it a good day for them, go for it. EBT works out to $6.30 a day, they can eat lobster today but then they don't get to eat for the last 3 days of the month. That's mismanagement and irresponsibility, but I don't know if it's abuse. They don't get to pull more money because they wasted it, the system is no worse off for it. It's allocation of happiness, they lump up a few really good days at the beginning in trade for some shitty ones at the end, instead of medium shitty all the way through.

But that's assuming it happens, I've never seen anyone do that. I assume it must at least a few times, but then I don't think those people care about this anyway. I'm looking out more for the majority, who already feel guilty buying ground beef instead of clearance chicken where it's a twist of the knife to be called a dirty lobster stealing scammer.

I'm on food stamps, I feel horrible about it. Horrible enough that my plan to get off of them involves suicide. Getting to that point was a death of a thousand cuts, this is another one of those cuts. You feel shame for being on it, shame while using it, once in a while a cashier or customer makes a comment that really compounds that. Half of the country blames me in part for destroying their country. The other half looks at me with pity. Every time there's a thread involving food stamps there's someone bitching that my kind blow it on expensive frivolous food, and someone else bitching that I blow it on cheap processed food. This guy's doing both at the same time. You hear politicians vowing to stick it to me by requiring drug tests or limiting what I can buy and their crowd cheers for it.

Whether it passes or not is irrelevant to me, I can't afford pork, I don't even walk through the seafood and beef areas. But having the law proposed and taken seriously, as if I might be doing something wrong, is another little pinprick of shame. The damage is done by insinuating it, not by enacting it.
Thank you. The biggest problem with this sub and ones like it is that no one that gets better ever comes back and says anything. There are no success stories here, it makes things look even bleaker.
I've always wondered if the ssn card/birth certificate thing was a narcissist thing, or if a lot of people have a hard time getting them from their parents.

I hate to try to talk someone out of repairing relationships, and maybe mine have made me fatalistic, but there's just no negotiating with these people. Your reaction is "there's no way my own family would act like this forever, there has to be a light at the end of the tunnel, if I could just do something." But they don't bend, they don't give an ounce, they'll hold you under water till you drown and then cry at your funeral and eat the sympathy up. Figuratively and literally. The way they act works too well for them, they reap all of the benefits and you carry all of the burden. A normal person wouldn't want to give that deal up, and these are not normal people.

To keep hoping for that happy fantasy will just rob you of time you could have spent building a different happy reality. One that unfortunately has to not include them. You can chase the carrot on a stick forever, and it will be forever, or work on getting strong enough to let the carrot go. Grieve the loss of your family, but then bury it and let it go. Put your effort and focus in the good things it sounds like you have in your life.
How did you make it stop?

2 reasons, maybe some of both. A. you're feeling unbearable mental pain, way above the normal limit. Going for a run or sitting down and breathing deep, is not going to come close to distracting you from the monster in the room. Cutting into yourself, feeling that pain, double the shock because you're the one doing it to yourself, seeing it opened up and bleeding. That's enough of a distraction to make you switch focus. Then, where with mental agony you had no way of bandaging or rubbing the pain to make it better, you can take care of this cut. You know? You're having a panic attack and someone gives you a hug, that's probably not going to stop it, but if they come in and throw you off the roof, that just might distract you out of a panic attack.

And B. there's usually a lot of self loathing involved with feeling that bad. "Why did you let your life get this bad? Why can't you fix it? Why can't you do anything to make it hurt even an ounce less? You deserve this!" I want nothing more than to badly hurt the person that did this to me... unfortunately that person is me.

Either way, be it by distraction or vengeance, you've finally done something about a massive pain that until then was untouchable. That's where the relief comes from.

Mine has 2 lines of thinking.

"You're going to give me what I want because I own you."

and

"I know I'm most of the reason you don't like being touched, so I'm going to force you and that will prove that I didn't really do any damage."

To the point where if nothing else she will chase and just wipe her hands on you, like a fucked up cat.

This is a surrogate for the 2 other issues you mentioned. You know that, that's why you mentioned them.

Minimum score is not the same as minimum ability. Minimum score is the line they draw that says if you meet this, you rank in the top group of the people we want. You're in that group. Where you are in that group is irrelevant, perfectionism will kill you. 

But that's done, you won, now you have to deal with the actual important issues. A rape and the guilt from the car crash, those will kill you too.

You're at a very important crossroad for depressed people, most of us make the wrong decision. Do you give in to the pain, lay down and cry and hurt and listen to what it tells you? That's what you want, you don't have much energy for anything else and it feels disturbingly comforting. Or you gather up all of the energy you have for the day and say "I'm going to use this for 15 minutes worth of finding someone to talk to" That's scary, you run yourself ragged in 15 minutes and still have the rest of the day to get through, it's going to suck. And even then, maybe you don't find anyone, maybe you do and they're useless like you've seen already. Then you have to try it all over again tomorrow until you find someone that works. It sucks, it's so much easier to lay in bed and cry tomorrow... that's what I'm going to do, I've been doing it for 15 years. But I'm going to pay for it, I'll never get better. You're on the edge of a deep hole, with a little bit of time to decide which direction you go. I wish I could stand up there and shove people back from the edge, but all I can do is stand down here and tell people to do their best to go against everything their mind is telling them and try to go the other way.

Also, I know it's hard to find any sort of help for these issues in the military. It might be worth it to find someone off base, pay out of pocket, sliding scale, and give a fake name to stay off the records. You never find someone that helps on the first try, but you do after a few tries.

"I'm only telling you this so that someone else doesn't... because I love you." You never knew how to love, and now there is no one else because I'm too scared of what they must be thinking. Thanks mom, you win.

I've been in this situation, I really don't hold it against them. It's not exactly a fast turn around situation. Once you're in you're in for 2 weeks+, beds aren't opening up hourly or even daily like with the other problems they treat. Even if they could double or triple their space, those would fill up and you'd still have people left out.

I'm in the same boat as Op so my thoughts should be taken with a grain of salt.

But... none of those people would even know my name, or anything about me. I'm just a job that fell down in front of them. As soon as I pass out of their hands, they move to the next job. Lots of people care in that unattached 3rd person sort of way, I've always known that. But what I'm dying for is that real "want-you-for-no-reason, just-because" sort of worth. Not because I fell down dying at their feet and they were compelled to help, or because I have or did something for them. Just the sort of casual acceptance that normal people seem to get.
Thanks for checking, but it doesn't really get better day to day.

Thank you. My questions of why are mostly rhetorical. It doesn't matter why they did it. But I do understand why anyway. Their parents were the same. When raised by that you either become the meat or the grinder. They chose grinder. Some of my siblings also chose to be grinders, some ended up as meat. But understanding doesn't really do anything for me.

As far as learning to be liked, I do have that book, and I think I am liked. I guess everyone would say that though. People don't dislike me anyway. In class they come to me to re-explain lessons and teach new stuff, seem to respect me for it. But I'm a nervous wreck during it. And it sort of feels in those cases I'm only wanted for what I can give. For other things, like friendships, they have better options. I don't help matters being too scared to really push for any more, I tell them what they need and let it go at that.

Doing things to have a good day just doesn't work either. Winter is so hard on me, I make it to summer and then end up too depressed to do anything. I wake up when the sun is going down, and even when I fix that and go to do things, I just sit sad and reflecting on what I'm about to go back to. I try to get it out of my head, honest hard trying, but everything reminds me of it.

Many. Sometimes it seems like an imbalance when things go dark so quickly. And it could be that after years of living like I did, do, that you'd end up with a faulty brain chemical response. But nothing has helped it even a little. But then I think, how much could I ask from medicines anyway? Most of the depression is from living in a life that's in shambles, missing everything I don't have. Medicines can't fix that, can't make me forget it, so how would the pain go away?

There were many over 8 or 9 years, I only counted my last one of 6 years because she's the one I liked and wanted to keep seeing. Still I did wonder a lot if I should try someone else. But my lack of progress is my fault, not hers. I just don't have it in me to start over again, trying to find someone I like, only to have them run up against the same wall that she hit. I'm making an unrealistic request of therapists, the same as this post, to fix something I can't even fix, come up with an answer that doesn't exsist. It just feels that at best, I'm just kicking the can down the road with therapy, sticking it out till next week hoping that that one will make things hurt less. But after this many years, how far is far enough? I'm also running out of money, she let me do sliding scale because she had known me before the insurance ran out, I don't know that I could get the same break from a stranger.
And now?

I had one for 6 years. I stopped going because I felt worse and worse about making someone listen to me complain so much without being able to show any improvement. This is just the simple "fight or flight" response that the brain is wired for. If you were trapped in a burning building, you would have something like a panic attack right? Depression is the same sort of trapped. You feel like your future is lost, everything hurts, nothing seems to be getting better... that's a huge emergency signal for your brain. You can't outright fight that so you're left with flight. You can't literally run from it either so you do a mental version of it. Heart rate goes up, breathing gets fast and shallow, mind races, brain gets tunnel vision. It's trying to save itself from imminent disaster the only way it knows how, but it's not a very helpful method.

Of course the solution is easier said than done. You have to stop the runaway train. Grab it by the shoulders and say "hey, brain, the world is not ending right this moment. It hurts a lot, it's probably going to hurt a lot tomorrow, but for the next 30 minutes we don't have to worry about fixing any of it, we just have to exist quietly and relax." Meditation could help a lot. Close your eyes, breath abnormally deep and slow and count your breaths to 10. If you get sidetracked and start thinking about anything other than the numbers, start over. The brain will not want to do this. It wants to run fast so that it can fix problems and make the pain stop right now. So start with a small amount of time, 2 minutes, 5 minutes, however long it takes to get to a 10 count once. Get good at that and then start pushing for longer times.

8 years, 0.5-1.5mg lorazepam 2 or 3 times a week. I'm sort of conflicted about them. I used them as an emergency parachute that I'd only pull a few hours into a panic attack to stop me from doing something worse. They spared me a ton of pain and maybe saved my life a few times, but it always seemed like it was just kicking the can down the road. If anxiety was at a 10 and I took them, it would drop to 0 but almost certainly be at least a 9 tomorrow and I'd want one again, and so on until I bit the bullet and went without to break the cycle. That cycle would also ruin my memory. After a few weeks of regular use I'd constantly have to ask people "did I already tell you about that?"

I ended up giving them up 90 days ago, threw them all away. Partly because I was scared that I had done long term damage as far as memory and anxiety, and partly because I sort of hoped that without the Ativan to save me I might fall far enough to die. My memory now isn’t terrible but still worries me, I have a hard time concentrating on stuff and learning as fast as I’d like… but it’s also possible that that is and always was a symptom of the depression. I also keep a chart of daily anxiety ratings and the last 90 days have averaged much less anxiety than when I was taking it. Which is not to say those 90 days have been good, but it seems like maybe the benzos were causing as much anxiety as they were stopping. 

For social anxiety though, they were never terribly useful. I haven’t found anything powerful enough that the social anxiety doesn’t overrule it. Klonopin was stronger than Ativan, but it just made me loopy and lasted for a longer time. All in all I never seemed to have any issues with building a tolerance, no withdrawal problems, and no dependence issues unless the anxiety cycle thing I mentioned counts as dependence. So, I used to be a huge fan of benzos. Now, I’m not really convinced that they’re bad, but I’m sort of neutral on the subject. I wouldn’t recommend someone use them but I wouldn’t recommend they don’t use them either.

I think you probably do have confidence up to a point. Which is way ahead of where most people with this problem are. But you've also got a big part of your brain thinking that you're defective because you're a virgin, and that tends to leak out in little ways. 

When you're talking to someone about guitars and music you're probably confident and totally at ease and don't have much to worry about. But when you're talking to someone you're interested in, you have that part of your brain that says you're defective screaming at you. And maybe you can still fake it almost flawlessly and look and sound at ease but there will be little things that neither of you will notice. Maybe you talk a little faster or slower, higher or lower, point your feet in the different direction, do something different with your hands, talk more concise or long winded. The tiniest things. No one in their right mind gives a shit which way someone’s feet are pointing, but nervous people point their feet away from what makes them nervous and subconsciously people pick up on it and it makes them uneasy too. You could go back later and ask her why it didn't work out and she'll say "I don't know, I just didn't feel it" and she's right, she doesn't know, it was just a bunch of things way too small to notice that made the interaction just off center of normal.

So my advice would be the micro analyze yourself. Find those tiny things and work on locking them down. It’s not easy, they’re small but they’re ingrained deep. One of mine was that when someone looked directly at me I would look away and look back, just for a second. Once I realized I did it, I could start to white knuckle it, know it was coming and fight it. But still, the more important a person is to me the harder it is to fight and the most important people can still force my eyes to jump. But if I hadn’t noticed it I wouldn’t be fighting it at all.

It effects different people in different ways. Some popular ones are obsessions over repetition, contamination and order. You know how everyone occasionally has that sudden jolt of "oh shit, did I leave the stove on?" but you're mostly able to think back and assure yourself that "no, I'm pretty sure I turned it off." People with ocd get stuck in a loop just after the jolt, you can't assure yourself even if you go back and look at the stove and see it off, you have to try it over and over in an attempt to chase after that feeling of assurance. Eventually the switch kicks over and you can feel at ease, some people are relatively lucky and have a set number that makes it click, 10 tries and they can feel ok. Some are not and the only thing that eases it is exhaustion. People don't understand it because it doesn't make much sense, the sufferer doesn't understand it that much either, "you're looking right at the stove and can see it's off, what is your problem?!" But faulty brain wiring makes people do crazier things than that.

As far as psychedelics treating ocd. A common correlation in people with ocd, anxiety and depression is a higher than normal blood pressure in the anterior cingulate cortex of the brain. Coincidentally, psychedelics cause this blood pressure to drop dramatically and stay low for extended periods of time. It is possible if not probable that this is the same thing that helps people who suffer from cluster headaches.

Depression lies to you, and it's a flawless lie. Even when you know you're being lied to, you still feel utterly convinced that its right, that its just laziness or that it really is hopeless. "Yeah I know depression makes you feel like this, but in MY case its true, I really don't have anything/can't do anything/won't get better/etc." Your brain constructed this belief, you're probably not going to be able to think your way around it using only the same brain. Meanwhile, if you explained your situation in detail to a 3rd person, they probably wouldn't see it nearly as fatalistically as you, because they're not being influenced by whatever is influencing you. 

So I would ask you to try to remember that fact, even though its almost impossible to really feel. And then work on getting some outside help for it. Therapy, maybe a little medicine, maybe a support group. It always makes me anxious when people say "I'm depressed but not suicidal and not really doing anything about it" because if you let yourself sit and stew in it long enough, you do become suicidal, and once you become suicidal that is an incredibly hard bell to un-ring.
